The task's 'a fifth to a half of the head silhouette' was an eyeball estimate of the face; as a pixel gate (2026-09-25) it invited solving the number instead of the gesture: in the v01 pose the hand lying entirely on the head covered 0.09-0.10 of the silhouette (slice/measurements/hand_over_head_attainable_2026-09-26.json), and the pose that did reach 0.2 (checkpoint 2) ran the forearm through the head — so the owner (2026-09-26) judges the eyes on the preview, hand_pose gates the anatomy, and this measure keeps 0.1-0.5 on every frame against a token hand (was 0.2-0.5). Measured on the render — the head re-projected from the exports against the forearm (object cryptomatte) and the hand (FOREGROUND_PLATE); bounding boxes overstated it on the SHOT_003 early checkpoint (28 % against 16 % measured). The number informs the owner, who judges the gesture

hand_pose.gesture: owner, 2026-09-26 (option 1): the hand comes from below and in front — the elbow down and forward at chest height, the forearm rising diagonally in front of the body, the palm on the eyes, the fingers towards the far temple; posed by hand as an animator does, with the numbers as a check, never as the target of a solver
hand_pose.basis: SHOT_003 v02 checkpoint 2 (2026-09-26): the hold solved numerically against the eye alone — elbow 206 mm above the shoulder, wrist 85 deg, forearm through the head (7/21 samples), hand 15 mm under the skin; the foreground plate lost 23 % of the hand to the head cut, which every order's head would show through. Limits: the elbow no higher than the shoulder joint (20 mm slack), the elbow 30-180 deg, the wrist within 50 deg, no hand pixel behind the head or the hair (0.5 % slack for the contact line), 5 mm of clearance from the head and the hair

three_quarter_neutral_rule: SHOT_003 is shot in 3/4 under neutral light, sadness and fear included (TASK §6 rule 4): it is the bake-off's only 3/4 material without the strong coloured light of SHOT_002, so its sadness, fear and hand_over_face windows keep the head at 35-55 deg to the camera on every frame — the three_quarter range. Added 2026-09-25: the SHOT_003 early checkpoint stood at 4-15 deg (frontal) and passed, because the rule lived only in the task text
head_angle_rule: angle in degrees between the socket's local +Z (the face direction, socket.json matrix_4x4 column 2) and the direction from the socket origin to the camera origin (camera.json position_m), both in socket space, centre sample of each frame
angular_velocity_rule: degrees per second between the centre-sample quaternions of consecutive frames: 2·acos(|q_i · q_{i+1}|) · fps; T = state_map.json → head_angular_velocity_threshold_deg_s, declared by the animator (burst 2 §6.3); rules that need T are NOT_EVALUATED until it exists

velocity_separation.rule: T must separate the tiers with a margin, not just sit between them: every MEDIUM-tier window (head_turn included) stays at or below medium_max_over_T · T on every frame, and fast_movement peaks at or above fast_peak_over_T_min · T on some frame — so the MEDIUM maximum and the fast peak are at least 1.5 / 0.8 ≈ 1.9× apart. The animator declares T with the triple (measured MEDIUM maximum, T, measured fast_movement peak) from check_states' own output, which prints the maxima while T is undeclared
velocity_separation.status: PROVISIONAL — ENGINEERING JUDGMENT (burst-2 Q18, 2026-09-17): without a margin T can be placed flush against the MEDIUM maximum and the MEDIUM / STRESS boundary of the bake-off would carry no meaning; the factors are recalibrated when the animator's first delivery exists
velocity_separation.context: head_turn has to cover ≥ 25° in its 24-frame window (≥ 25°/s mean, ~50°/s peak with ease-in/out), so T sits well above 50°/s; the export's continuity ceiling (quaternion dot > 0.99 between frames, ~390°/s) bounds the fast peak from above

freeze_rule.note: a run of more than this many consecutive frames in which no channel and neither the socket position nor its rotation changes is a freeze (burst-2 ACCEPTANCE item 3); measured per shot over every frame

jump_rule.measure: the step between consecutive frames is the median, over every vertex of default_head_rest.obj, of the vertex's screen displacement when the head is placed by the socket's centre sample of the earlier and of the later frame, both seen through the LATER frame's camera at the video profile's pixel intrinsics — the head's own motion, not the camera's
jump_rule.rule: a step is a single-frame jump when it is more than ratio_over_both_neighbours_max times BOTH neighbouring steps and more than floor_px. A short smooth move (two or more large steps in a row) and a laugh bounce are not jumps; a pose that changes by a whole step in one frame between calm frames is
jump_rule.status: PROVISIONAL — calibrated 2026-09-24 on the contractor's SHOT_001 v01 and SHOT_002 v01 (slice/measurements/shot_002_v01_acceptance_2026-09-24.json): the four real jumps (discontinuous per-window pose formulas — SHOT_002 1153, 1177, 1195; SHOT_001 1019) measure 4.1–5.5×, every other step of both shots, both laughs and SHOT_001's 4-frame glance-follow included, at most 2.08×. The floor is a noise guard for near-static frames (1.5 px at 1080p), not a visibility threshold. A designed single-frame accent is declared in QUESTIONS.md with its frame and decided by the owner
